<!-- docs-drift-check -->
### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **5** package(s): `@objectstack/mcp`, `@objectstack/metadata-core`, `@objectstack/rest`, `@objectstack/runtime`, `@objectstack/spec`, touching **55** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/runtime/test-typecheck-debt.json`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**21** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 14754c70cf460357a21b1d37519d4e7a2fa03a4d`.

⛔ **9** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/runtime/test-typecheck-debt.json`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **1** cross-cutting symbol(s) contributed no route anchor: `resolveObjectMasker (5 routes)`
- **4** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **247** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **182** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **182**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **123** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **182** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 14754c70cf460357a21b1d37519d4e7a2fa03a4d` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `1c18d561f579c33197560bafc298b203c928aa8e` — the merge of head `f18e2ae7bdb3085adb0fef10e4eb984098734cc1` into base `14754c70cf460357a21b1d37519d4e7a2fa03a4d`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 1c18d561f579c33197560bafc298b203c928aa8e && git checkout 1c18d561f579c33197560bafc298b203c928aa8e
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 14754c70cf460357a21b1d37519d4e7a2fa03a4d f18e2ae7bdb3085adb0fef10e4eb984098734cc1 && git checkout -B drift-repro 14754c70cf460357a21b1d37519d4e7a2fa03a4d && git merge --no-ff f18e2ae7bdb3085adb0fef10e4eb984098734cc1

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 14754c70cf460357a21b1d37519d4e7a2fa03a4d
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 14754c70cf460357a21b1d37519d4e7a2fa03a4d` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `77dc5621370acaa6c376911d0074377ba68ab666`
Local-runs: none
Scope: docs/adr/0106-metadata-plane-fls-object-schema-masking.md + .changeset/meta-object-read-visibility.md, scripts/adr-anchors/packages__metadata-core__src__object-schema-fls.ts.json, packages/metadata-core/src/object-schema-fls.ts, packages/metadata-core/src/object-schema-fls-contract.ts, packages/rest/src/meta-item-read-gate.ts, packages/rest/src/meta-item-read-routes.ts, packages/rest/src/meta-item-history-routes.ts, packages/runtime/src/domains/meta.ts, packages/runtime/src/domains/mcp.ts, packages/mcp/src/stdio-data-bridge.ts

### ① Derived judgments

- **Ruling match.** Ruling 6787890900 on #32004 was read by REST GET. Amendment bullets 1, 3 and 4 restate it. Bullets 2 and 5 go beyond the ruling; ④ judges them.
- **Declarations.**
  - `Clause-②: yes (narrowing)` and `Metadata-protocol: none` are present, and the same in the PR body and the changeset.
  - The BREAKING banner and one ADR-0087 marker are present.
- **No published schema moved.** `packages/spec` is untouched; the only governed hit is the ADR.
- **Check-runs at this head.** 30 runs, none failed. Several jobs were still in progress when read.
- **Outlets that hold, by reading.**
  - REST list and plain item read
  - published and diff reads
  - the app bundle
  - runtime list, published and legacy reads
  - HTTP MCP `list_objects`, `describe_object` and `validate_expression`
  - the stdio bridge

  Each leaves the object out, or answers with the door's unknown-name answer.
- **Exemptions hold.** D8 and the D4 exemptions, system context included, are decided before the object question. No over-refusal of an author or of the system context was found.
- **Validators hold.** The REST plain read answers absence before any validator is judged. The list validator is computed over the served list.

### ② Semver level

`patch` on the four moved packages is the level AGENTS.md prescribes for a non-protocol breaking change. The exported posture union gains a member, and the mask result gains a required flag; the BREAKING banner covers both. No level finding.

### ③ Boundary flags

| Flag | Judgment |
|---|---|
| (1) Action doors judge only the field half | Follow-up, not a blocker. The changeset states the carve-out; the amendment is silent on it (S4). |
| (2) Object admission folds a fault into "no" | Blocks the published claim (M3). |
| (3) Console nav entries are not pruned | Follow-up (S3). |
| (4) An outlet bearing object names is not narrowed | Follow-up, but the PR does not disclose it (S3). |
| (5) No new ETag fold | Holds. No 304 or validator oracle was found. |

### ④ Design judgment

**must-fix**

- **M1. An outlet is left out.** One by-name object read under the metadata path, on both transports, asks no per-caller verdict. It answers an unreadable object differently from an unknown name. [detail held by the security seat]
- **M2. A hidden answer is not identical to the unknown-name answer.** On the layered read and on the runtime plain item read, the store is read before the absence verdict. For an object in one stored state, that read answers differently from the REST plain read. This contradicts "no two outlets can disagree". [detail held by the security seat]
- **M3. Amendment bullet 5 is not what is enforced.** The security service's object admission fails closed to "no" by contract. So an evaluation fault inside it is answered as absent, not as 503. Either the amendment, the changeset and the PR body state what is enforced, or the mechanism changes under a ruling. The seat should also judge the D6 tier-2 window. [detail held by the security seat]

**should-fix**

- **S1.** A security service without the object admission member hides nothing, with no telemetry. Neither the changeset nor the amendment names this tier.
- **S2.** D7 is narrowed without saying so. A caller with no principal, or with no resolved permission set, is now served no object, and the changeset's restore path does not exist for that caller.
- **S3.** Outlets that bear names and labels are neither narrowed nor recorded as known residuals. [detail held by the security seat]
- **S4.** The amendment omits the action-door carve-out that the changeset states.
- **S5.** The operator docs for the D8 switch still describe field masking only.

**nit**

- The tier-2 telemetry reads "serving the unmasked schema" for an object that is then answered as absent.
- Amendment bullet 3 adds "the D8 switch" to the ruling's text.
- D5's outlet list is not updated.

Implemented-by: `claude/sec2-r3cw`
Reviewed-by: `session_01QSeKYn5CmmdShCJifm6WYj`

**VERDICT: FAIL**

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `41fc49ea679e29ab3c230bb6ea132468c970d4a9`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/api/rest-server.zod.ts, docs/adr/0106-metadata-plane-fls-object-schema-masking.md + .changeset/meta-object-read-visibility.md, packages/metadata-core/src/object-schema-fls.ts, packages/rest/src/meta-object-state-routes.ts, packages/rest/src/rest-server.ts, packages/runtime/src/domains/meta.ts, content/docs/deployment/environment-variables.mdx, content/docs/deployment/production-readiness.mdx, content/docs/references/api/rest-server.mdx

Delta record: `77dc562137..41fc49ea67`, against the FAIL record on `77dc562137` (comment 6796962773).

### ① Derived judgments

| Finding | State | Basis |
|---|---|---|
| M1 — state read left out | closed for the object rule | Both transports resolve the caller's posture first and answer the door's own no-object answer before any registry read. See M4 for what the ADR now says about this door. |
| M2 — hidden answer before any store read | **open in one case** | Closed on the layered read (both spellings, both transports), the runtime published read, the legacy exit and the runtime plain read with no member named. Reopened by deviation (d). |
| M3 — text states the fail-closed behaviour | closed | The amendment, changeset and PR body now say a fault folded into "not admitted" is answered as absent, and only an admission that throws is the 5xx fault. |
| S1 — service without the object admission | accepted deviation | Still narrows nothing, but is now stated in the amendment and changeset and said at warn. Whether that satisfies the security contract's "absence is not admit" is the seat's call. |
| S2 — D7 narrowing unstated | closed | Amendment and changeset state it. |
| S3 — name and label outlets | closed as disclosed | Listed as known residuals in the amendment and changeset; not re-graded. |
| S4 — action-door carve-out | closed | The amendment states it. |
| S5 — operator docs for the D8 switch | closed | Three docs pages and the spec TSDoc say the switch also governs object visibility. |
| Tier-2 telemetry nit | closed | The notice now names what the caller is answered. |

**Check-runs at this head:** 72 runs, none failed; one duplicate `Check Changeset` run was still in progress when read. All Test Core and Test UI shards, the type-check jobs and the Governed Surface Queue Guard are green.

**Dogfood:** the Dogfood Regression Gate on this head is green only as an aggregate; its shard job was skipped, so CI has not run the battery on this head. The last local run was on `77dc562137`, before the runtime doors changed order. A local re-run is owed on the head that fixes the items below. Otherwise the merge-queue shards are the first run of it.

### ② Semver level

Unchanged: `patch`, BREAKING banner, both declaration lines and the ADR-0087 marker are present. The spec file changes comments only; no schema output moves, and it sits in the fixed version group with a package the changeset already bumps. No level finding.

### ③ Boundary flags

| Deviation | Judgment |
|---|---|
| (a) Short-circuit also on the runtime published read and legacy exit | Acceptable. Same rule, same door-own answer, pinned. Nit: each of these two doors now asks the posture twice per request, so a tier-2 notice is said twice. |
| (b) S5 through spec TSDoc and a regenerated reference, no spec changeset | Acceptable, for the reason in ②. |
| (c) Missing-admission warning once per service instance | Acceptable. |
| (d) Runtime plain read skips the short-circuit when a member is named | **Not acceptable.** See M2. |
| (e) State door resolves the posture first, so an unevaluable read answers 503 there | Acceptable. It is the D6 tier-3 answer every other object door gives, and the changeset lists the door. |

The four residuals already escalated to the seat were not re-graded.

### ④ Design judgment

**must-fix**

- **M2 (still open) — deviation (d) leaves one store answer reachable.** With a member named, the runtime plain read hands an unreadable object to the store. The store's own refusal for an object in one stored state is raised before the member is judged. That caller is answered that refusal, while a missing name is answered the member refusal. The stated justification, "refused for every name alike", does not hold for that state. The changeset and PR body now claim "before the store … is consulted" for this door, and the new pins do not cover a named member. Removing the exception gives the same answer as the REST plain read. [detail held by the security seat]
- **M4 (new) — D5 item 5 claims more than the state read enforces.** The new ADR text lists the state-machine read among outlets "brought under the same projection". That door applies the object rule only: for a readable object it still answers about a field the caller may not read. Either the sentence says the door applies the object-level rule alone, or the door enforces the field projection. [detail held by the security seat]

**should-fix**

- None new.

**nit**

- The double posture ask under (a), above.
- Amendment bullet 2, "no two outlets can disagree", is true again once M2 is closed.

Implemented-by: `claude/sec2-r3cw`
Reviewed-by: `session_01QSeKYn5CmmdShCJifm6WYj`

**VERDICT: FAIL**

## Contract review

Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/api/rest-server.zod.ts, docs/adr/0106-metadata-plane-fls-object-schema-masking.md + .changeset/meta-object-read-visibility.md, packages/runtime/src/domains/meta.ts, packages/runtime/src/domains/meta-disabled-package-doors.test.ts, packages/rest/src/meta-disabled-package-doors.test.ts

### ① Derived judgments

The delta is two commits, five files: `e82c4187e5` (runtime plain read, pins on both transports) and `6ce51e3a92` (ADR and changeset text). No spec file and no other outlet moves. Read outside the diff, not reviewed: the REST plain read, the posture resolver, and the security service's object admission.

| Finding | State | Basis |
|---|---|---|
| M2 — hidden answer before any store read | **closed** | The runtime plain object read now answers an unreadable object with its missing-name answer before any store or registry read, whether or not a member is named. This is the order the REST plain read already had. Both transports pin a named member: the answer equals the missing name's, and neither the by-name read, the cached read (REST), the layered read nor the registry is asked about the object. |
| M4 — D5 item 5 over-claims the state read | **closed** | D5 item 5 no longer lists the state-machine read among the projected outlets. It now says that read applies the object-level rule only. The amendment's residual list and the changeset both name its field level as a known residual. This matches the code on both transports. |
| Nit — double posture ask on the runtime published read and legacy exit | closed | Each of the two doors now resolves the posture once per name per request and reuses it for the projection, so a tier-2 notice is said once. A rejection is reused too, which keeps the answer the same within the request. |
| Nit — amendment bullet 2 | reworded, see ④ | The outcome it states is true again. The mechanism it now adds is stated too widely. |

**Ruling match.** Unchanged from the earlier records: lists leave the object out, a describe answers as an object that does not exist, author exemptions and reference fields are untouched. The delta narrows nothing beyond the ruling.

**Fixture change.** Both transports' security doubles changed from admitting every object but one to admitting one object alone. The comment gives the reason: the real service does not admit a name with no object behind it. That was read in the security service and holds. The new named-member pins depend on it; see ④.

**Changeset against code.** The changeset matches the code at this head, including the new residual.

**PR body against code.** The body was not updated for these two commits; see ④.

**Check-runs at this head:** 68 runs, 58 success, 10 skipped, none failed, none in progress. `Check Changeset` and the Governed Surface Queue Guard are green.

**Dogfood:** the `Dogfood Regression Gate` aggregate is green, but its shard job and `Dogfood Verify CLI` were skipped, so CI has not run the battery on this head. The last local run recorded on the PR is on `77dc562137`, two rounds back. The local re-run the previous record asked for is not recorded. The runtime door order changed again in this delta, so the merge-queue shards remain the first run of the battery over this code unless the seat records one.

### ② Semver level

Unchanged: `patch` on four packages, BREAKING banner, both declaration lines and the ADR-0087 marker are present. The delta changes no exported type and no schema output. No level finding.

### ③ Boundary flags

| Flag | Judgment |
|---|---|
| Deviation (d) of the previous record | Removed. The exception is gone from the code and from its comment. |
| The state read's field level is declared a residual instead of being enforced | Acceptable as a disclosure. The ruling's bullet is about objects a caller cannot read; a readable object's field level on that door is outside it. Whether that residual needs its own card is the security seat's call. [detail held by the security seat] |
| Fixtures now model a service that refuses unknown names | Acceptable; it is what the shipped service does. The dependency is not written down anywhere a third-party service author would read it. Follow-up, see ④. |
| Author | PR `user.login` is `objectstack-fleet[bot]`; no separate author note is owed. |

The residuals already escalated to the seat were not re-graded.

### ④ Design judgment

**must-fix**

- None.

**should-fix**

- **S6 (new) — amendment bullet 2 states an order that only the by-name reads have.** The new sentence says every schema-serving outlet answers the object verdict "before it reads any store". That holds for the by-name object reads on both transports. The lists, the MCP tools and the stdio bridge read their listing first and then leave the object out or answer their unknown-name answer. Their outcome agrees with the by-name reads, so the conclusion ("no two outlets disagree about whether an object exists for the caller") holds; the stated mechanism does not. The sentence should claim the order for by-name reads only. The changeset's second bullet carries the same wording. This is governed text, so the fix moves the head and owes a delta.
- **S7 (new) — the PR body is stale against this head.** Its known-residuals bullet omits the state read's field level, which the ADR and changeset now carry. Its verification section still names `41fc49ea67` as the branch head and reports pin counts taken there. Its test list does not mention the named-member rows. A body edit closes this without moving the head.

**nit**

- The named-member equality depends on the security service not admitting a name that has no object. The shipped service satisfies this. The object-admission member's contract text does not state it. A one-sentence addition there, or a pin, is a follow-up. [detail held by the security seat]
